audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 9, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness and historical audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for conditional temple promise, land-loss theology, Tyrian cities, Gezer conquest and civilian killing, forced labor by ethnicity, military class distinction, Pharaoh's daughter, maritime expertise, and gold extraction.

verses.restored: When Solomon finished building house of YHWH, king's house, and all Solomon desired and delighted to do,
YHWH appeared to Solomon a second time, as appeared to him at Gibeon.
YHWH said to him, I heard your prayer and plea made before me. I consecrated this house you built, putting my name there forever; my eyes and heart shall be there all days.
If you walk before me as David your father walked, in wholeness of heart and uprightness, doing all I commanded and keeping my statutes and judgments,
I will establish throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I spoke to David your father: A man shall not be cut off for you from throne of Israel.
But if turning you or your children turn from following me, do not keep commands and statutes I placed before you, and go serve other gods and bow to them,
I will cut Israel from face of land I gave them, and house I consecrated for my name I will send from my presence; Israel shall become proverb and taunt among all peoples.
This house shall become a ruin/high place; everyone passing shall be astonished and hiss, saying, Why did YHWH do thus to this land and this house?

They shall say, Because they abandoned YHWH their Divine, who brought their ancestors from land of Egypt, grasped other gods, bowed to them, and served them; therefore YHWH brought all this evil upon them.
At end of twenty years, in which Solomon built two houses—house of YHWH and house of king—
Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with cedar, cypress, and gold according to all desire. King Solomon then gave Hiram twenty cities in land of Galilee.
Hiram went out from Tyre to see cities Solomon gave him, and they were not right/good in his eyes.
He said, What are these cities you gave me, my brother? He called them land of Cabul until this day.
Hiram sent king one hundred twenty talents of gold.
This is account of forced labor King Solomon raised to build house of YHWH, his house, Millo, wall of Jerusalem, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, captured Gezer, burned it with fire, killed Canaanites living in city, and gave it as marriage gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Lower Beth-horon,
Baalath and Tamar in wilderness, in land,
all store cities Solomon had, chariot cities, horseman cities, and all Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and all land of his dominion.
All people remaining from Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not children of Israel—
their descendants remaining after them in land, whom children of Israel were not able to devote to destruction—Solomon raised them as forced labor levy until this day.
But from children of Israel Solomon made no slave laborers; they were men of war, servants, officials, officers, commanders, chariot officers, and horsemen.
These were chiefs of officers over Solomon's work: five hundred fifty, ruling over people doing work.
Pharaoh's daughter went up from City of David to her house Solomon built for her; then he built Millo.
Three times in year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings upon altar he built for YHWH and burned incense before YHWH. He completed house.
King Solomon made a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber beside Eloth, upon shore of Reed Sea, in land of Edom.
Hiram sent in fleet his servants, seafarers knowing sea, with servants of Solomon.
They came to Ophir, took from there four hundred twenty talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.

translation_notes: The temple promise is conditional. Sacred institutions can be abandoned when covenant practice collapses; holiness is not institutional immunity.
The explanation of land loss through religious failure is ancient theological interpretation and must not be used to blame displaced or colonized people for their own dispossession.
Solomon gives twenty inhabited Galilean cities to Hiram within a royal exchange. The residents' consent and political status are absent.
Gezer is captured, burned, and its Canaanite residents killed before becoming a marriage gift. This is conquest, mass killing, and transfer of land—not a neutral building note.
Surviving non-Israelite peoples are conscripted into hereditary forced labor. Ethnic hierarchy and slavery are explicit features of Solomon's state.
Israelites are spared slave status but militarized and absorbed into royal administration; unequal privilege does not equal freedom from extraction.
Tyrian sailors contribute specialized knowledge to the fleet. Ophir's gold reflects distant extraction and trade whose workers and communities are unnamed.
Pharaoh's daughter appears again through palace location and marriage diplomacy rather than her own testimony.
safety_note: Do not use covenant warning to blame victims of war, displacement, famine, or institutional collapse. Do not sanitize Gezer's destruction, ethnic forced labor, land transfers, militarization, or gold extraction as prosperity.
